problem: Lehmer's conjecture on the Mahler measure of non-cyclotomic polynomials
missing_details: Domain specification: P(x) is a polynomial with integer coefficients in Z[x]
Exact definition of the Mahler measure M(P) as |a₀|∏ᵢ max(1,|αᵢ|) for roots αᵢ
Definition of 'non-cyclotomic': P not an integer multiple of a product of cyclotomic polynomials or a monomial
Precise form of the conjecture: existence of an absolute constant μ>1 such that every non-cyclotomic P satisfies M(P)≥μ
Equivalence between the multiplicative form M(P)≥μ and the logarithmic form m(P)>c
refined_question: Does there exist an absolute constant μ>1 such that for every non-cyclotomic polynomial P(x)=a₀∏_{i=1}^D(x−α_i) with integer coefficients a₀,a₁,…,a_D∈ℤ, its Mahler measure defined by M(P):=|a₀|∏_{i=1}^D max(1,|α_i|) satisfies M(P)≥μ?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, does there exist c>0 such that for every polynomial P(x)∈ℤ[x] that is not a product of cyclotomic polynomials or a monomial, the logarithmic Mahler measure m(P)=log M(P) satisfies m(P)>c?
justification: The name indicates the conjecture involves Mahler measures of non-cyclotomic polynomials but omits domain (integer polynomials), precise definition of Mahler measure, and the existence statement of a uniform lower bound μ>1. The refined question incorporates all necessary definitions and faithfully restates the canonical existence claim from the Wikipedia article. The equivalent formulation is drawn from the explicit logarithmic version in the Motivation section.
